title: Bounded Prime Gaps: Dense Clusters and Sieve Reduction
description: Formalizes structural consequences of the Maynard-Tao bounded prime gaps theorem: dense prime clusters in bounded intervals, generalized gap telescoping, and sieve reduction lemmas. Proves that gaps sum to p_{n+m} − p_n. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Zhang (2013) proved that lim inf(p_{n+1} − p_n) < 70,000,000. Maynard-Tao (2014) improved this to 246 and proved infinitely many prime clusters in bounded gaps: lim inf(p_{n+k} − p_n) < C(k) for explicit C(k). This file formalizes structural consequences: gap sum formulas, dense cluster implications, and reduction to sieve bounds.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize: (1) Telescoping sum Σ primeGap(n+i, i<m) = p_{n+m} − p_n. (2) Dense cluster implications of bounded gap results. (3) Sieve reduction lemmas.
overview.proofStrategy: gap_sum_range: telescoping sum by definition of primeGap. Dense cluster: if gap bound ≤ H, then among m consecutive primes, any interval of length H·m contains all of them. Sieve reductions: relate prime gap density to sieve admissibility.
keyInsights: **Gap telescoping**: Σᵢ₌₀^{m-1} primeGap(p_n + i) = p_{n+m} − p_n. This is a simple telescoping identity but fundamental to cluster analysis.
**Dense clusters**: If liminf(p_{n+1} − p_n) ≤ H, then infinitely often, m primes lie in an interval of length H·(m-1). Maynard-Tao: H = 246 for all m.

**Sieve admissibility**: A k-tuple (h₁,...,hₖ) is admissible if it doesn't cover all residues mod p for any prime p. Admissibility is necessary (but not sufficient alone) for the tuple to contain infinitely many prime tuples.

sections.mathContext: Admissible k-tuples: no residue class covers all of $\{h_1,...,h_k\}$ mod $p$ for any prime $p$.

conclusion.summary: Bounded prime gaps sieve theory: 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Gap telescoping, dense cluster implications, sieve reduction all proved.
conclusion.implications: These results provide formal infrastructure for reasoning about prime gap clustering. The gap telescoping identity is fundamental; combined with the Zhang/Maynard-Tao bounds, it enables quantitative statements about prime cluster density.
openQuestions: Can the Maynard-Tao bounded gaps theorem (liminf(p_{n+1}−p_n) ≤ 246) be formally proved?
Can the Green-Tao primes in arithmetic progressions theorem be formalized?
Can the twin prime conjecture (liminf = 2) be resolved formally?
